Audi Q9 Debuts World's First Curved Digital OLED, Panel Thin as a Human Hair
18 photos
Photo: Audi
Not that long ago, car lights moved from being used to make the road ahead visible during the night to becoming a symbol of status and, in certain circumstances, communication tools with the exterior world. They are, if you will, smart lights, and they appear to become even smarter as time goes by.
Audi is one of the carmakers that has always been at the forefront of R&D in the field of vehicle lights, having implemented, for instance, OLED technology on the Audi TT RS about a decade ago. It has continuously tried to make that tech better, and here's the latest version of Audi's car lights, coming in a form never seen before in the industry.
Before getting into it, a quick reminder of what OLED (organic light-emitting diode) is: a semiconductor light source that uses stacked layers of organic molecules to recombine electrons in various ways once a voltage is applied.
In the version announced this week, Audi's digital OLED technology hides all that underneath one of the thinnest glass surfaces around. That would be only 0.1 millimeters thick, which is about the same as the thickness of a human hair.
Using such panels allowed Audi to bend the assembly on a radius of up to 200 millimeters, closely following the contours of whatever car it is fitted on. In this case, that would be the new Q9.
Audi calls the launch of this hardware on the big SUV a technological world first. For the driver, other drivers, and perhaps even pedestrians, the solution not only makes the Q9 visible from the back and from the sides, but can also be used to communicate things depending on what the OLED shows using semi-active digital light signatures with 3D effects.
As used on this vehicle, the OLED consists of 512 segments placed on six panels. Among them, the curved outer panel made of 99 segments, the middle one with 84 segments, and an inner panel with 73 segments. All of this makes this one the largest OLED panel Audi has ever produced so far.
The tech supports up to eight digital light signatures, which can be shown, for the first time, in a semi-active fashion, making them particularly striking, especially in the dead of night.
Audi did not say when the tech will expand to cover other models in its lineup, but we'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more about that.
As for the Q9 that's involved in this evolution of rear lights, the luxury SUV starts on the American market at $118,000 for the SQ9 version. It's unclear at the time of writing whether the curved OLED lights will be included as standard or offered as optional extras.

Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat Races R35 Nissan GT-R, Someone Wins the Fight By Just One Mile Per Hour
14 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Once again, we have been waiting in vain: it’s already been a decidedly long time since the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube have not yet returned to their traditional venue - Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey. Instead, they’re still into roll races.
Instead of feisty quarter-mile dragstrip skirmishes, we’re getting 65-mph roll race battles – this time around between a crimson L-bodied Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat packing the iconic 6.2-liter supercharged Hemi V8 and a serious gray R35 Nissan GT-R, with the Godzilla relying on its legendary 3.8-liter VR38DETT twin-turbocharged V6 engine.
Enticed by something else other than the countless prepped surface quarter-mile battles they have witnessed over the years, the videographer keeps showing us that roaring V6 and V8 engines are best witnessed at the highest speed possible – all thanks to the continued high-speed ‘drama’ happening at the legendary Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania.
This place has been around sine 1969 and has seen just about everything, including major events like NASCAR, the IndyCar Series, and the IMSA GT Championship series. This time around, we are dealing with one of the smaller gatherings. That doesn’t mean they’re uninteresting, especially RaceMotive’s 65-mph roll race series. So, while we wait for new quarter-mile dragstrip battles, the videographer shows us high-speed clashes between iconic models, like this Hellcat and GT-R .
The protagonists have been presented, so let’s kick off the action with a roaring initial skirmish: both cars felt like they were glued next to each other, and at the end of the first skirmish there was less than one mph between them: 144.88 mph for one of the protagonists and just 145.09 mph for its opponent. The loser quickly asked for a rematch, and it was promptly granted.
So, they went at it again, and they went neck-and-neck all over again. Believe it or not, the separation was once again breathtaking: the winner had a top speed of 152.36 mph while the runner-up posted a 151.33 mph pass! Now, let’s check out the video and find out who’s who!
By the way, the R35 Nissan GT-R has become a relic of the past after production ended last summer. It did have a lengthy run, with manufacturing starting in December 2007 and the grand tourer getting a ton of upgrades over the years, culminating with the GT-R50 that celebrated half a century for the GT-R nameplate.
Meanwhile, the Dodge Charger nameplate is alive and well, offered in eighth-generation form, although fans do miss one thing: the mighty V8. The current STLA Large-based Charger fastback coupe and sedan are only offered as the Daytona with an EV setup or as the Sixpack models featuring the 3.0-liter twin-turbo inline-six Hurricane engine.

Johannes Ariens sells hydrogen semis, and he thinks the push to clean up trucking is aimed too high. Incentive programs and the broader industry are fixated on Class 7 and 8 tractors, said Ariens, CEO of Range Zero Emissions, in an interview with FreightWaves. The trucks ready to go electric today are medium-duty Class 4, 5, and 6 models, he said.
Range Zero Emissions is a dealer group that sells only zero-emission commercial vehicles. Its brands run from Zero Motorcycles up to Class 8 trucks, and it has no tie to Range Energy, the electric-trailer company that shares its name.
The lineup grew in August. Range became an authorized dealer for Hyundai’s XCIENT Fuel Cell, a hydrogen Class 8 truck, with Washington as its primary territory. It also folded Ziegler Truck Group’s zero-emissions business into the Range brand and bought the West Coast operations of Ethero Truck & Energy. Together the two deals moved the company from one Pacific Northwest location into the Midwest and California, Ariens said.
Most commercial truck users run medium-duty trucks, he said, and many of them can charge on the kind of power a small business already has.
“Charging two vehicles on Level 2 is like, do you have a washing machine and an air compressor at your house? If you do, you can install two Level 2 chargers and charge them overnight and go to work every day for your shift,” he said. “You’re good to go if you’re driving less than 150 miles a day.”
The case for medium-duty trucks first
Ariens describes electrification as a progression, from e-bikes and small cars like the Chevy Volt up to Rivians and the Hummer EV. Each step built charging the next one could use.
“We are so focused on Class 7 and 8 that we’re trying to jump a very natural progression of electrification,” he said. “You cannot charge a Class 8 semi on a Level 2. It literally won’t do it.”
Class 8 charging is still early. Tesla, which formally opened its Semi factory in Sparks, Nev., on Sept. 24, expects more than 30 Megawatt Charging System stations by the end of the year.
“It’s years until that’s proliferated, and until all the legacies jump in,” Ariens said.
Medium-duty trucks already have big buyers. “We’ve got FedEx, we’ve got Rivian, we’ve got Amazon,” he said. In September FedEx ordered 2,000 all-electric trucks from Harbinger , one of the brands on Range’s roster.
Most of trucking’s own ranks are small: of nearly 580,000 active U.S. motor carriers, 91.5% operate 10 or fewer trucks, according to American Trucking Associations data drawn from U.S. Department of Transportation figures as of June 2025. FreightWaves has reported on that long tail . Ariens would steer more voucher money their way.
“We should increase the voucher amounts for Class 4, 5 and 6,” he said. “Just get all these small businesses with five trucks or less into their EVs.”
State incentive programs that refill
Federal support for zero-emission trucks is pulling back, Ariens said, at the same time California and Washington run “the most significant medium- and heavy-duty commercial incentive programs in history.”
California’s Clean Truck and Bus Voucher Incentive Project, known as HVIP, has delivered more than $1 billion since its 2009 launch, according to Gov. Gavin Newsom’s office. In May the state added the California Clean Fuel Reward, a rebate for electric medium- and heavy-duty trucks with $250 million available this year and more than $1 billion expected through 2030, funded by the Low Carbon Fuel Standard. FreightWaves broke down how those programs stack in June. Washington launched its Zero-Emission Incentive Program on April 29 with $112 million in vouchers from the state’s Climate Commitment Act.
“These are continuous, recycled funding streams, usually coming from carbon tax credits, designed to refill,” Ariens said. “They’re not one-shot programs.”
Many commercial fleets replace trucks on a five- to seven-year cycle, he said, and a program that refills fits how they buy.
“I’m not going to buy a new truck and get rid of it next month because I want an EV,” he said. “I’m going to life-cycle that truck, get my full depreciation out of it, and then cycle it.”
Once a technology reaches 5% of new adoption, Ariens said, it tends to stick.
“That’s exactly what these government incentive programs are designed to do: help get from zero to 5, which is very hard,” he said.
Where hydrogen fits in Class 8
Ariens calls the battery-or-hydrogen debate binary thinking.
“I think the future of Class 8 is absolutely both,” he said.
Battery-electric works for drayage , he said, because port trucks need less range and can carry a smaller battery. Weight is the trade-off: federal law gives battery-electric trucks a 2,000-pound allowance on the power unit, up to 82,000 pounds gross. Every added pound is a pound of freight the truck cannot haul, Ariens said.
Hydrogen is starting at ports too, because trucks there run consistent daily routes from a single fueling point. Ariens named Long Beach, Oakland and the Vancouver area as the main places a heavy-duty hydrogen truck can fuel today. Shell built a heavy-duty station at the Port of Long Beach, according to the California Energy Commission , and HTEC opened a station for Class 7 and 8 fuel-cell trucks at the port terminal in Delta, British Columbia, in June.
The 30-truck NorCAL ZERO project runs XCIENTs in drayage out of the Port of Oakland and launched in May 2024 , according to the California Fuel Cell Partnership. Ariens watched those trucks at a Port of Oakland event in September.
“Those trucks were going by all day, in and out. No big deal,” he said. “Then those trucks are going 300, 400 miles, and it’s, ‘Cool, let’s put one of these in Sacramento.'”
The XCIENT has also moved east. Hyundai’s Metaplant near Savannah, Ga., began running 21 of the trucks in December 2024, and a Rutgers-led pilot at Port Newark in New Jersey planned to start testing six in early 2026, according to Transport Topics .
For all of that, Ariens keeps returning to the smaller trucks.
“That’s my party line, and the thing I stomp my feet about every day,” he said. “Why are we not making it as easy as possible to go to Class 4, 5 and 6, and then Class 7 and 8 will solve its own problem?”

Honda Racing Releases Its First-Ever In-House Made Parts for the Civic Type R and Integra Type S
13 photos
Photo: Honda
It's been almost two years to the date since Honda Racing Corporation (HRC) announced during the 2024 SEMA show it is officially entering the performance parts business, and we were kind of losing hope of seeing that anytime soon. Luckily, this year's SEMA is fast approaching, and with it so do the first HRC parts designed in-house.
The company decided to start its adventure into this segment with new sets of forged wheels and a tuned exhaust system. These parts are meant to be used on a number of higher-spec Honda and Acura models, including the Civic Type R, Integra Type S, and Passport TrailSport.
There will be two new wheel sets available for the cars mentioned above. The first set, intended for the 2023 and newer Honda Civic Type R and the 2024 and newer Acura Integra Type S, comes in at 19 inches and is made of aluminum.
The wheels have been designed by Honda with help from Italian company 2elle-engineering, which supplies the wheels for the ARX-06 race car. Fitted with thin spokes, the wheels can be had in either gray or bronze.
What makes these wheels special is the fact that they weigh almost 21 pounds (9.5 kg), and that can have a serious impact on the way the Hondas they are meant for handle and perform while on the track.
The second wheel set is a tad smaller, coming in at 18 inches. Made of forged aluminum, these bits of hardware are meant to be used in off-road settings, meaning they have been specifically designed for the 2026 Honda Passport and the 2023 and newer Honda Pilot .
They were made with assistance from Titan 7, which supplies the wheels for Honda Racing's Pikes Peak International Hill Climb and other production-based race car efforts. Compared to the factory wheels fitted on the two SUVs, they can handle 220 pounds (100 kg) more load.
Last but not least, HRC is introducing next month at SEMA a new, tuned cat-back exhaust developed together with Borla. The stainless-steel piece of hardware is designed for the same Passport and Pilot models, and it is supposed to increase both their performance and sound.
The exhaust comes with six percent more flow rate and is fitted with Borla's so-called polyphonic harmonizer that boosts the sound of the double-overhead cam 3.5-liter V6 it can be tied to. As a twist, it is also smaller than the factory one, and that translates into a ground clearance increase of some 1.9 inches (five cm).
Honda Racing will bring these new parts to the SEMA show at the beginning of November, where it will also preview the next parts that will enter the catalogue later on: among them, adjustable coilovers with camber plates, a big Brembo brake kit with 6-piston callipers, and a short-throw shifter.

The V16 Plug-In Hybrid Bugatti Tourbillon Would've Been Fully Electric if VW Had Got Its Way
61 photos
Photo: Bugatti
The automaker known as the Volkswagen Group used to control Bugatti. It all started in 1998, when the Wolfsburg-based colossus acquired the French automaker's design and naming from Romano Artioli. Indeed, the guy who commissioned a Bugatti factory in Italy for the EB110. In 2021, the Porsche division moved the company into a joint venture with the Rimac Group.
Porsche and the Volkswagen Group as a whole completely sold off remaining stakes in Bugatti Rimac earlier this year, giving the hypercar marque to the Rimac Group and HOF Capital. As the German automaker was planning its divestment of Bugatti, the suits in Wolfsburg pressed Mate Rimac to develop a fully electric successor to the Chiron.
It sure was time for something completely new, especially if you remember that the Chiron follows the very same recipe as the Veyron. Even though Mate Rimac had the Nevera's platform ready to fulfill this project's non-negotiable targets, the guy in charge of Bugatti Rimac and the Rimac Group opted for something far more daring than VW's idea.
Mate Rimac went in the opposite direction, building the Tourbillon around a Cosworth-developed naturally aspirated V16 that happens to be larger than the Volkswagen Group's quad-turbo W16 engine. Instead of complete electrification, the compromise reached with the Volkswagen Group came in the form of plug-in hybrid assistance. This compromise also helped the Tourbillon meet Euro 7 regs, but more importantly, an internal combustion engine this ludicrous gives the car emotional appeal.
Speaking to Automotive News, the Croatian engineer and entrepreneur made it clear that he originally believed that electric powertrains would become preferable to internal combustion in the hypercar segment due to inherent peak torque and software advantages. The Nevera, however, taught Mate an uncomfortable lesson in regard to how emotion works in the automotive industry.
Photo: Bugatti More specifically, the very technologies and advantages that once made electric hypercars feel like the future also took away something extremely important. With the passing of time, said technologies and performance attributes became the norm across multiple segments, hindering the appeal of electric hypercars. Customers at the top of the market, he concluded, do not settle for the norm.
Mate compared the shift to the world of luxury watches. Remember when digital watches were once viewed as futuristic? They eventually became commodities, and buyers returned to the appeal of traditional analog timepieces. The parallel was clear for Mate, and you can also see a bit of this parallel in the absolutely insane gauge cluster of the 1,775-horsepower Bugatti Tourbillon.
The chief exec acknowledged that developing a completely new hybridized powertrain would be far more complex and costlier than going electric while leaning on the Nevera's platform, but looking back, Mate and company have nothing to regret. The originally proposed Bugatti electric hypercar might have bombed hard, and bombing hard is not an option at this level of the industry.
Mate was equally candid to Automotive News about the commercial outlook for the Nevera itself. Asked whether he would start the Croatian electric hypercar program today, Mate would still explore the potential of four independently controlled electric motors, because why not? But from a commercial standpoint, he acknowledged that it would be the wrong choice in 2026.
That admission makes the Tourbillon decision all the more revealing. Mate isn't arguing that electric powertrains lack performance or that Bugatti should abandon new technology. Instead, he is arguing that technical capability is a very different animal from customer appetite. As it often happens in this business, they do not always move in lockstep.

The 2027 Aura Beachy 420 Is a Compact Travel Trailer With an Unusual Layout and Cool Features
22 photos
Photo: Hobby Caravan
The RV equivalent of "how much you can do with a tiny thing" is the Beachy 420, one of the four flooplans available in the Beachy series of travel trailers – or caravans, as they're called in Europe. The Beachy 420 is perhaps the best choice for an example, since it's a family-friendly unit in a very small form factor.
It's not the tiniest out there, to be sure, but it might be if you consider its versatility and extended functionality. The Beachy 420 is the first entry in the Beachy series that offers real family-friendliness, with a super-size king bed at the back that will fit three adults or two adults and as many as two kids.
And that's not even the most impressive thing about the Beachy 420. That would be its versatility, its openness and degree of comfort, and the vibe that's perfectly matches its name and intended purpose. Out of all compact caravans in Europe, the Beachy is perhaps the most stylish and beautiful.
The Beachy line was launched German specialist Hobby in 2021, first as a concept and then as production models for the 2022 year. For 2027, Beachy is making a move across the pond, getting its official launch in the UK at the 2026 Motorhome & Caravan Show at NEC Birmingham, where the video tour at the bottom of the page was shot.
Photo: Hobby Caravan It won't be called Hobby Beachy , though, but Aura Beachy. Aura is "A brand for Britain [but] made in Germany," the name under which Hobby will be selling products here. An Aura Beach is the same Hobby Beachy that's been a fan favorite across Europe for years, but in slightly different, Aura-branded clothes.
Not that this should stop us from taking the Beachy 420 in – or revisiting it, if you're already familiar with it.
"Could you do with a little bit more?" Hobby asks in the presentation for the Europe-bound Beachy 420, before promising more storage space and one additional berth, both of which they deliver. The Aura description of the UK variant is less enticing , but with a product as nice as this one, it probably doesn't even have to be that.
Photo: Aura Campervans The Beachy 420 is built on a single-axle KNOTT chassis, with an overrun brake with automatic adjustment, hitch stabilizer, shock absorbers, and extendable heavy-duty corner steadies. It's licensed for highway use (for up to 100 kph/62 mph) and it's built with bonded sandwich panels for frameless structural integrity, GRP underfloor, and double-glazed tinted windows that open awning style.
The 420 floorplan comes in at 5.68 meters (18.6 feet) overall length, with 4.26 meters (14 feet) for the body and a width of 2.16 meters (7 feet). It's compact but not very small by European standards , but it's the only one to offer dual entries and cargo hauling capabilities.
The Beachy 420 has an extra-large entry door on the campsite side and a tailgate-style opening in the rear wall panel. This last one doubles as a loading area for gear, including larger items like motorcycles and bikes, which can be stored between the two benches at the back and secured with the provided tie-downs.
Photo: Hobby Caravan At camp, this opening is your oversize window onto whatever view you happen to be parked by, a way of inviting the great outdoors inside and a quick way out whenever you feel like it.
That's another thing that makes this caravan different from the rest, its outdoorsy character. Like its name says, the Beachy isn't designed to be lived in full time; it's more of a durable and cozy tent on wheels that will get you to the beach and provide you with an above-the-ground basecamp.
That explains its modularity and what could be perceived as a lack of basic creature comforts. The Beachy 420 is intentionally basic so you may spec it with exactly the things you need, and none of those you have no use for.
Photo: Hobby Caravan The kitchen space, for instance, is a mere worktop with a sink with only cold water and a larger slider drawer with a 12V cooler box underneath. Located at the very front of the trailer, it offers plenty of counter space for whatever appliance you want to bring along and sufficient storage for foodstuffs, pots and pans, and cutlery.
The closet angled to the side is both storage space and a rudimentary washroom in the 2027 UK version. It comes standard with a porta-potti and a large mirror, but also adjustable shelves and hanging space, so if you don't mind going number 2 under your finest beach dresses (or shirts), you will not have to rely on campground bathroom facilities when nature calls.
The rear of the trailer is taken up by two large benches in a face-to-face disposition. During the day, that's your dinette if you add the freestanding table, or your lounge. At night, you can use the space in several configurations: as twin beds, a double bed, or the super-size king that takes up the entire floorspace here.
Photo: Hobby Caravan As promised, the Beachy 420 offers ample storage options , in addition to the cabinets and open cubbies in the kitchen and the large closet slash toilet room. You also get two large pieces of furniture with fabric organizers and elasticated cables, and overhead cubbies on both sides. These come with more boxes and cables, so you can choose one you like best when packing.
The Beachy 420 comes with one-key locking system, a 25-liter (6.6-gallon) tank for freshwater in the closet, a rollable tank for wastewater, 12V, USB, and USB-C outlets, an opening skylight over the bed/living space, and beautiful pendant lights.
The European version offers options like a weight upgrade, a drawbar bike rack, special Beachy decals, a weather-proof aluminum storage box on the drawbar, a 230V electric heater with 1kW output, and pre-wiring for solar, and it could be that they will be available for the Aura variant as well. The textile boxes are optional in Europe, as is the toilet.
Photo: Hobby Caravan The Beachy 420 has an empty weight of about 842 kg (1,856 lbs) depending on options and a maximum permissible weight of 1,000 kg (2,204 lbs), which can be upgraded to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs). The Aura variant will also come with Aura-branded upholstery and throw pillows in a nice golden sand color.
The unit brought to the trade event and toured below had a sticker of £20,995, which is roughly €25,100 or $28,100 at the current exchange rate.

Jeep Reveals Everything That's New About The 2027 Wrangler: Paints, More Features, Special Editions
12 photos
Photo: Jeep
The specialty US automaker wants to talk about the 2027 Wrangler at large, clearly revealing all the novelties for the new model year, including the pricing and order details.
Stellantis is busy picking up the pieces after the previous business strategy proved to be pernicious, and the new management is putting all the brands on the right track – although some faster than others. Jeep, for example, is of utmost importance for the North American division, and has received its need fair share of attention.
Unfortunately, a recent hazardous material spill incident forced an evacuation at the Toledo Assembly Complex, where Jeep manufactures two of its most important models, including the Wrangler, which sees the light of day in the North Plant. Alas, that doesn’t mean they stopped revealing the novelties.
So, after explaining everything that’s new about the 2027 Jeep Cherokee, now it’s time to find out all the juicy details about the 2027 Wrangler. The 2026 model year has 13 models available to configure, starting with the two-door Sport at an MSRP of $36,035 (sans the destination of $1,995) and concluding with the Moab 392 kicking off at $79,995.
Now, the 2027 model year roster starts from $36,635 for the same Sport 2-Door model, and now there are only 11 models to configure, right up to the Moab 392, which has unchanged pricing. The novelties for the 2027 model year include the Wrangler Sport, Sport S, and Willys models featuring a standard 7-inch TFT color instrument cluster, while Sport S and Willys also add standard passive entry.
Also, the two-door Willys receives the same standard vented power dome hood as the four-door model, while the Sahara trim level now has standard McKinley trimmed seats, side steps, a nine-speaker Alpine premium audio, embedded navigation, rear park assist, blind spot and cross path detection, auto-dimming rearview mirror, auto high-beam headlights, universal garage door opener, and a front off-road TrailCam.
The Rubicon adventurers gain standard heated front seats, a heated steering wheel, as well as embedded navigation. Most importantly, five of the Jeep Wrangler Twelve 4 Twelve special editions will remain available for the 2027 model year: Moab 392, Willys 392, Whitecap, Rewind and Rockslide. Coming with late availability, there’s a host of new exterior colors: Gobi, Sting Gray, Hella Yella, plus the limited-edition Fathom Blue, while first-ever paints Ghost and the limited-edition Gum 31 make their debut.
Under the hood, the Jeep Wrangler has three powertrain options. The base is the 2.0-liter inline-four turbo mill with 270 horsepower and 295 lb.-ft. of torque, paired only with an eight-speed auto. The intermediate option is the 3.6-liter V6, naturally aspirated, with 285 hp and 260 lb.-ft. of torque, paired with a six-speed manual transmission or the eight-speed automatic gearbox. Last but not least comes the mighty 6.4-liter (392ci) Hemi V8 engine packing 470 hp and 470 lb-ft of torque.

source_document.body:
2026 Paris Motor Show • OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
2026 Mazda3 and CX-30 Receive Thorough Upgrades in Australia, Including New Grades and Features
14 photos
Photo: Mazda
The Japanese automaker's local division in the Land Down Under wants to make the Mazda CX-30 subcompact crossover SUV and the Mazda3 passenger car irresistible for enthusiasts.
Mazda Australia recently decided to make Mazda MX-5's rivals green with envy with the latest updates for the 2026 model year for the iconic sports car, received a five-star ANCAP safety rating for the all-electric Mazda 6e as well as the latest CX-5, made the six-cylinder hybrid diesel and the plug-in hybrid models more affordable across the market, and also confirmed the pricing and specification for the all-new Mazda CX-6e all-electric crossover SUV, so we can say it has been pretty busy in the Land Down Under.
Well, the work never ends, and now they are announcing the “abundance of meaningful updates applied for 2026” to the “widely popular” Mazda3 and Mazda CX-30 – with the latter headlining the changes with the addition of not one but two new trim levels: CX-30 G25 Evolve SP and CX-30 G25 GT.
Starting with the 2026 Mazda CX-30 G25 Evolve SP, the new grade builds upon the Evolve model and adds black cloth seats with red stitching that’s also available on the armrest, center console, and dashboard. Outside, the Evolve SP has a sporty focus with gloss-black trim on the 18-inch alloy wheels, exterior mirrors, roof rails, and badges.
On the other hand, the new CX-30 G25 GT focuses on a premium atmosphere with a glass sunroof, black leather interior, heated front seats, and a 10-way powered driver’s seat with position memory. Outside, there are 18-inch silver alloy wheels, silver roof rails, body-colored mirrors, and silver badging. Both grades use the G25 Skyactiv-G powertrain and come with advanced keyless entry.
All G25-powered CX-30 models now get a standard Vision Technology package featuring a 360-degree View Monitor with See-Through View, Cruising & Traffic Support (CTS), Driver Monitoring, front parking sensors, Front Cross Traffic Alert (FCTA), and Front Cross Traffic Brake (FCTB). It’s also standard on the Mazda3, but only from the Touring grades upward.
Additionally, the CX-30 G25 GT SP debuts White Maztex seats with grey synthetic suede inserts, and also comes with the same gloss-black exterior highlights as the Evolve SP. From now on, the CX-30 GT SP and Astina grades also have ventilated seats, added for the first time across the CX-30 model range. Both the CX-30 and Mazda3 now have a standard 10.25-inch Mazda Connect screen, and it comes with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto across the family.
The safety department adds Smart Brake Support (SBS) on the Mazda3 and CX-30 – it now detects motorcycles, turn across traffic, and head-on collisions; there’s also intersection collision avoidance assist. The Mazda CX-30 range gets access to the newly introduced Zinc Green Metallic premium paint; Aero Grey Metallic is available for both the CX-30 and Mazda3, while the Ceramic Metallic and Zircon Sand Metallic are biting the proverbial dust.
“The Mazda3 and CX-30 continue to be important models within our line-up, offering our customers a compelling combination of award-winning design and engaging driving dynamics – and with the latest updates, we’re adding even more value into the equation,” said Jarrod Gieschen, Director of Sales and Marketing at Mazda Australia .
The updated Mazda3 and Mazda CX-30 are available to order; deliveries will start before the end of the month, and pricing kicks off at AU$31,910 (MLP) or about $22,401 at the current exchange rate for the Mazda3 sedan and hatchback, while the CX-30 has a starting point of AU$34,760 or over $24k.

WELLINGTON, New Zealand — The Chief of the New Zealand Defence Force, Air Marshal Tony Davies, has informed Defense Minister Paul Goldsmith that he is resigning his role.
Arrangements are underway to transition responsibilities to the Vice Chief of Defence Force, Rear Adm. Mat Williams, who will serve as Acting Chief of Defence Force.
Air Marshal Davies said: “The resignation is for personal reasons, and results from errors of judgement made by me in the past, for which I am taking responsibility. The errors of judgement were contrary to the values of the Defence Force.
“These matters revolved around an inappropriate relationship I had when in a position of unit command, and I regret not disclosing this when I had the opportunity to do so.”
Appointed as the Chief of Air Force from 2016 before becoming the Vice Chief of Defence Force in 2018, Air Marshal Davies, born 1966, was promoted to his current rank on appointment to Chief of Defence Force on June 6, 2024.
The Chief of Army, Maj. Gen. Rose King, will act as Chief of Defence Force until Sunday before Williams takes on the role.
About Nick Lee-Frampton
Nick Lee-Frampton is the New Zealand correspondent for Defense News.

James May Is Selling the Triumph Stag Featured in the Final Episode of The Grand Tour
17 photos
Photo: Collecting Cars
There is probably no better time to be a fan of the former Top Gear and later The Grand Tour trio, as two of its members, Jeremy Clarkson and James May, are getting rid of some of the cars they own.
We've already had a look at no less than three vehicles Clarkson owns, namely a Lancia Montecarlo Spider, an Alfa Romeo GTV6, and a Lincoln Continental Mark V. These rides are scheduled to go under the hammer with no reserve in mid-November.
Now, we learned of a vehicle owned by James May doing the same, only this time as part of an online auction. Not just any vehicle, true, but one we don't cross paths with very often: a 1974 Triumph Stag MKII.
The 2+2 sports tourer has been around for a very short period of time back in the 1970s, as a mix of British mechanical expertise supplied by Triumph and styling handled by Giovanni Michelotti, known for his work with Ferrari, Lancia, and Maserati.
May became the owner of the car almost three years ago, and he seems to have been so impressed with it that he even featured it in the final special of The Grand Tour , One for the Road. He now has it listed as an object of an online bid on Collecting Cars.
The car is far from being in perfect condition, despite having gone through two restorations before May got his hands on it. With over 83,000 miles (134,000 km) on the clock, it shows its share of wear and tear.
There are misaligned panels here and there, patina on some of the interior elements, trim pieces that may need to be replaced, pitting on some chrome components, and dashboard lights that have seen better days.
Other than that, though, the Stag is in pretty good condition, with the original naturally aspirated 3.0-litre V8 still on deck to drive the rear wheels, aided by a four-speed manual transmission. Both the powertrain and the suspension system have been overhauled at some point in the past.
Although this is a car owned by James May, there is one unexpected connection with the third member of the former Top Gear crew, Richard Hammond. Remember how I said earlier the car has been through two restorations? Well, during one of them, the Stag got its magenta exterior color at the hands of The Smallest Cog, the restoration business that climbed to fame as part of Richard Hammond's Workshop TV show.
Propped on 14-inch, five-spoke wheels shod in Hankook Optimo tires, the Triumph carries an interior in black packed with a three-spoke steering wheel, door card pockets, a Kienzle analogue clock, Smiths gauges, and a retro-style stereo with Bluetooth connectivity as a touch of modernity.
The Triumph Stag owned by James May is selling online, with six or so days left until bidding closes at the time of writing. The most someone is willing to pay for it right now is £13,500 ($18,000).

2026 Paris Motor Show • OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
All-New Toyota Land Cruiser EV Renderings Put the Electric CUV Right Next to the Off-Road SUV Boss
6 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Japanese automaker is doing a lot of things lately: testing their next mid-engine coupe, recalling J250-generation Land Cruisers for a fuel leak fire risk, trying to convince the European Union that some hybrids are actually zero-emission models, or potentially fitting the next Corolla generation with ICE, hybrid, and full EV powertrains, among other things – like updating its American models to the 2027 model year standards.
Just recently, though, Subaru did one interesting EV thing without the help of its all-electric model partner, Toyota. More precisely, they built a 510-hp electric wagon featuring dual motors, lighter hardware, plus an integrated control unit to show how its EV platform could evolve and reach the next generation of all-wheel drive models.
So, it’s no wonder that Toyota also has a new EV – though only across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI and courtesy of the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators. More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on a new Toyota – the Land Cruiser EV.
The new model is being developed based on the Land Cruiser Se concept and could be introduced around 2027, though maybe not in America , where the latest iteration of the Highlander, now completely electric, has been recently postponed due to the grim prospects of the EV market in the United States.
Nevertheless, the rumor mill believes that development is ongoing for a launch next year, complete with a new unibody architecture that till clearly set it apart from both the current J250 and J300 Land Cruiser models. It will probably focus on family versatility and city driving, rather than the great outdoors. Many outlets expect it to feature a five- or seven-seat arrangement to clash with rivals like the Kia EV9, and while initial models will arrive with current battery packs, the Land Cruiser EV could also serve as Toyota’s debut model for high-performance solid-state battery options.
Anyway, the pixel master doesn’t have much to say about the dual-motor all-wheel drive powertrain options – he’s more preoccupied with showcasing the all-new, first-ever Toyota Land Cruiser EV in his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project based on the newest spy photos. The design features a new styling ethos for the Land Cruiser, with slim LED headlights, a boxy side profile that’s wide and muscular but also more streamlined than the ICE and hybrid SUV siblings, plus a rear featuring a simple look underpinned by a new full-width LED taillight signature.
Last but not least, perhaps to better understand the upcoming design changes, the CGI expert also drops the newly rendered Toyota Land Cruiser EV based on the latest spy shots alongside the round-headlight version of the current Toyota Land Cruiser (Prado). 2026 Paris Motor Show • Project KO11 Is Proof That Geely Wants To "Knock Out" Range Rover, Launches Next Year in Europe
Honda Confirms 2028 Body-On-Frame Pickup Truck Derived From Mitsubishi's Triton
13 photos
Photo: Mitsubishi
Mitsubishi's Laem Chabang complex in Thailand is theoretically capable of churning out 420,000 vehicles a year. Said industrial estate produced roughly 170,000 vehicles in 2025, which is just around two-fifths of its capacity. Going forward, that empty space will be partly filled by a Honda-branded truck.
The larger of the two Japanese automakers recently signed a memorandum of understanding to sell a body-on-frame midsizer based on the Triton, with sales planned to start in 2028 for ASEAN markets. Will that Mitsubishi -derived Honda truck be sold in the United States and Canada? We don't know for sure yet, and chances are it won't because the Triton's underpinnings were not developed with North America in mind.
Honda intends to beautify its yet-unnamed truck with dedicated stylistic touches, meaning that everything under its body panels will be shared with the Mitsubishi. The larger partner calls the arrangement complementary supply, and certain numbers reveal a few background details behind this complementary supply.
From the standpoint of Mitsubishi, output at the Thai production complex slid from a little over 310,000 vehicles in 2021 to 170,000 in 2025. Part of that nosedive is attributed to the Triton, which dropped to 82,766 deliveries worldwide last year. By producing a badge-engineered truck for Honda, the agreement raises plant utilization.
Regarding Honda, the second-largest Japanese automaker after Toyota doesn't really have experience with body-on-frame trucks. The Ridgeline it produces in the US for North America is best viewed as a crossover posing as a truck, and a unibody at that. Developing a body-on-frame truck would have cost Honda a whole lot of money, and Honda knows how difficult it is to deliver a truly compelling midsizer from the poor-selling Kia Tasman for the Aussie market.
Photo: Mitsubishi Brazil Making only minor changes to the styling of the Triton also makes a whole lot of sense because Honda recently booked its first loss since going public in 1957. The reported $2.6 billion deficit is tied to an extremely poor electric vehicle onslaught and the collapse of its Chinese business.
Speaking of China, both Japanese brands are fully aware that Chinese newcomers have carved into their share across Southeast Asia. From this standpoint, it's easy to understand that Mitsubishi sees the Honda order as a way to enhance the bottom line. This memorandum of agreement dates back to an August 2024 merger plan that included Nissan.
Talks did collapse after Honda proposed taking full control of Nissan. Two years later, this pickup is the first tangible product of the surviving agreement. While the proposed merger is of no relevance anymore, the trading is. Honda is also weighing mutual vehicle supply with Nissan in North America, and rumor has it that body-on-frame models are of interest to Honda in this part of the world.
Could that mean the revived Xterra could also get a Honda-badged sibling? We'll have to wait and see, but that's easy to imagine. After all, even Nissan used Mitsubishi's Triton for its fourth-generation Navara. And just like Honda's mid-size truck for ASEAN markets, the 2026 model year Navara is related to the all-new Pajero. As The Weeknd once said during his mixtape era, this is a happy house, and we're happy here.
